quals-wisconsin-algebra-1999s-02.title: Right ideals
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1999s-02.body:

**(i)** Submodules of $R_R$ are exactly the right ideals of $R$. If $R$ is a division ring and $I
e0$ is a right ideal, it contains a unit $u$, so $I\supseteq uR=R$; thus $R_R$ is simple. Conversely, let $R_R$ be simple and $0
e x\in R$. Then $xR$ is a nonzero submodule, so $xR=R$ and $xy=1$ for some $y$. Then $y
e0$, so similarly $yz=1$ for some $z$. Hence $x=x(yz)=(xy)z=z$, so $yx=1$ and $x$ is invertible. So $R$ is a division ring.

quals-wisconsin-algebra-1999s-03.title: Extending the isomorphism $\alpha\mapsto\beta$
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1999s-03.body:
Fact: if $E\subseteq\mathbb{C}$ is finite Galois over $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\tau\colon F\to\mathbb{C}$ is a field embedding of some $F\supseteq E$, then $\tau(E)=E$ (normality).

**(i)** Let $F\subseteq\mathbb{C}$ be the splitting field over $\mathbb{Q}$ of $g=f\cdot h$, where $E$ is the splitting field of $h\in\mathbb{Q}[x]$. Then $\alpha,\beta\in F$ and $E\subseteq F$. Since $f$ is irreducible, there is an isomorphism $\sigma\colon\mathbb{Q}[\alpha]\to\mathbb{Q}[\beta]$ with $\sigma(\alpha)=\beta$. $F$ is a splitting field of $g$ over both $\mathbb{Q}[\alpha]$ and $\mathbb{Q}[\beta]$, so $\sigma$ extends to an automorphism $\tau$ of $F$. Then $\tau(E)=E$ and $\tau(\mathbb{Q}[\alpha])=\mathbb{Q}[\beta]$, so $\tau(\mathbb{Q}[\alpha]\cap E)=\mathbb{Q}[\beta]\cap E$ ($\tau$ is a bijection of $F$). Hence these fields are isomorphic via $\tau$.

**(ii)** If $E=\mathbb{Q}[\varepsilon]$ with $\varepsilon$ a primitive $m$th root of unity, then $\mathrm{Gal}(E/\mathbb{Q})$ embeds in $(\mathbb{Z}/m)^\times$ and is abelian. So every subgroup is normal and every intermediate field of $E/\mathbb{Q}$ is Galois over $\mathbb{Q}$. In particular $D=\mathbb{Q}[\alpha]\cap E$ is Galois over $\mathbb{Q}$, so $\tau(D)=D$ by the fact above. By (i), $\tau(D)=\mathbb{Q}[\beta]\cap E$. Hence $\mathbb{Q}[\alpha]\cap E=\mathbb{Q}[\beta]\cap E$. ∎

quals-wisconsin-algebra-1999s-04.title: One-dimensional eigenspaces
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1999s-04.body:
Let $n=\dim V$ and let $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n$ be the $n$ distinct roots of the characteristic polynomial of $S$ (it splits since $F$ is algebraically closed). Each $\alpha_i$ is an eigenvalue with eigenvector $v_i$; eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues are independent, so $v_1,\dots,v_n$ is a basis and each eigenspace $E_{\alpha_i}=Fv_i$ is $1$-dimensional.

**(i)** Let $v$ be an eigenvector of $S$, $Sv=\alpha_iv$, so $v\in E_{\alpha_i}=Fv_i$. Since $ST=TS$, $S(Tv)=T(Sv)=\alpha_iTv$, so $Tv\in E_{\alpha_i}=Fv$, i.e. $Tv=\beta v$ for some $\beta\in F$. Thus $v$ is an eigenvector of $T$.

**(ii)** By (i), $Tv_i=\beta_iv_i$. If $T^k=0$ then $\beta_i^kv_i=0$, so $\beta_i=0$. Hence $T$ kills the basis $v_1,\dots,v_n$, and $T=0$. ∎

quals-wisconsin-algebra-1999s-05.title: Composition length
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1999s-05.body:
**(i)** Let $\theta\colon V\to W$, $\theta(v)=(v+M_1,\dots,v+M_n)$. It is an $R$-homomorphism with $\ker\theta=\bigcap_iM_i=0$, so $V\cong\theta(V)\subseteq W$.

**(ii)** Write $W_i=V/M_i$. The chain $0\subseteq W_1\subseteq W_1\oplus W_2\subseteq\cdots\subseteq W_1\oplus\cdots\oplus W_n=W$ has factors $\cong W_i$, which are simple, so it is a composition series and $W$ has length $n$. Hence $\theta(V)\cong V$ has finite length $\le n$, and so does $W/\theta(V)$, with $\ell(V)+\ell(W/\theta(V))=n$.

For each $i$, the chain $0\subseteq M_i\subseteq V$ refines to a composition series of $V$ whose top factor is the simple module $V/M_i$; by Jordan–Hölder, $V/M_i$ is a composition factor of $V$. The $V/M_i$ are pairwise nonisomorphic, so $V$ has at least $n$ composition factors (counted with multiplicity): $\ell(V)\ge n$. Therefore $\ell(W/\theta(V))=0$, i.e. $\theta(V)=W$, and $V\cong W$. ∎
